Name: Alloyrun
MemoText: GTW64 Note: ----------- A nice little sideways SEU created by the well respected Ashley Routledge and Dave Saunders (Ash and Dave). Featuring some neat (if strange) parallax scrolling and graphics, this game isn?t that bad at all.  Although it?s no Armalyte, its a good game and also features a great little title screen, with a band playing to the title tune? typical of Ash and Dave styled demos. Jeroen Tel also provided some of his first C64 music for the game to add to the polish of a strong little game.  Originally, the game wasn?t going to be called Alloyrun, but in fact had an initial name as Antaeus. But after finding out that this was in fact a brand name of an aftershave, the name was scrapped quickly in favour of their second name, ?Alloyrun?.  In its original Antaeus form, the game was submitted to Firebird for evaluation ? but they rejected the game. In the end, Starlight would pick up the title and was to become the eventual publisher.  Although the game was actually completed and ready for release, Starlight ran into financial difficulties and were unable to pay Ash and Dave for their efforts. Therefore, both Ash and Dave would not let Starlight release the game until they were paid. This never happened, and the game was canned.  It?s believed that Ash and Dave then, with no other publishers, released the game onto the scene for the sake of it. However, neither could recall doing so ? so it seems it was leaked by someone within the scene.  Recently in 2016, whilst digitally preserving Ashley Routledge?s work disks, a build of Alloyrun in the form of Antaeus was found fully working. It includes temporary Rob Hubbard tunes from Ace 2 and Firebird logos. It is probably the version that was pitched to Firebird. The game itself isn?t too different from the final version, but is a nice curiosity to see.
V_Comment: also includes preview and demo version

Name: Blockie
MemoText: CF version is corrupt: - The intro scroller turns corrupt after a while.  - The game SID goes of sync horribly   ----------  GTW64 Note:  The first time I heard of this nice looking Columns clone was from its release on Commodore Format?s Power Pack 37. It was listed as a PD game, and came from Hex Heroes public domain. However, it firstly wasn?t PD at all ? and was also incomplete too!  I never noticed at the time, but when you run ? there?s a crack intro from the group ?Awesome?.  Back in 1991, many different cracking crews had released a preview of the game and it seems it snuck into a PD library by mistake.  What is particularly funny is that the CF team clearly didn?t play the game that much, apart from to set some instructions and get some screenshots. The game is playable to a degree, but the score and bonus doesn?t work ? and the game never actually ends.  Once it fills up with blocks, they just continue to drop.  The question now though is about who was behind the game, and what happened exactly. Was it intended for commercial release and did it ever get any further than this?  What is interesting is that what looks like an earlier preview has been out there for some time called Futris (short for Future Tetris), which doesn?t include any of the status panel areas. It also doesn?t clear the blocks like with Blockie ? suggesting that Blockie may have been someone trying to tidy up the Futris preview and finish off.  However, confusingly the Futris preview is from 1996 and not 1991 ? so had this just been an earlier build of Blockie leaked at a later date when under a different name?  Talking about the game with Richard, it inspired him to have a go at tidying the game up and fixing some of the issues to actually make it properly playable. So, to fix the block disappearances, to make the game properly end and for all the scoring to work. Essentially ? to try and finish the game off as much as possible.  After several months on and off, and with some testing work by Dirk S. and Simon Quernhorst, Richard finally finished his reconstruction work for Games That Weren?t. There might still be the odd glitch, but it is already in far better shape than it was all them years ago for Commodore Format readers.

Name: Co-Axis
MemoText: Co-Axis was Jason's first real game (further information on the predecessors and the evolution that lead to Co-Axis can be found at his blog) but the final version was never properly released back in the day; during development, a preview copy sent to a couple of software houses for evaluation was trained and spread by Rough Trade Inc., which effectively killed the project dead.  When that crack turned up online a decade later, Jason decided to set things straight and this release came about, built from a later development copy which was then extensively modified and fixed release. Five real trainers were fitted (rather than the claimed four of the previous release), several bugs were patched and a fix added to make sure everything worked on the early revision C64. This release also includes the final loading screen, which was previously unseen.  To play Co-Axis, connect a joystick to port two, directions move the ship around and the trigger fires the primary weapon. To pause the game, press run/stop (unless that key has been reassigned by the trainer) and to quit, press Q.  Trivia: There's a cheat-mode in the game itself, type 'the secret garden' (a song by T'Pau) on the titles page to become invincible.

Name: Cyberwing
MemoText: Nobody is quite sure where the aliens came from, but the have ransacked our galaxy and left a trail of destruction through five colony structures. All communication with Earth has been cut, we have no way of warning them. Your mission is to take remote control of a Cyberwing Mk. 3 mid-range fighter and navigate through the five colonies to get a message through, taking out as many enemy fighters as you can on your way.  To assist you the Cyberwing Mk. 3 has a standard issue plasma cannon and has been fitted with five particle disseminator destructors (or mattersplatter bombs). The man cannons can be activated with the trigger on your control stick and a mattersplatter is fired with the spacebar. The mission can be paused at any time with the run/stop key (fire restarts) and aborted with the Q key.  Should the Cyberwing be destroyed we have two more units that can be beamed in to carry on the fight and extra units will be assigned as you prove yourself worthy of the resources. Good luck commander, a Cyberwing is ready for immediate launch.  Review: 'This is the kind of game where everyone will compete to get the highest score rarther than get to the highest level. A solid game which shoot-em-up fans should enjoy.' Max Maslen, Total 64  Trivia: There's a built in cheat, type 'janet fielding' (the actress who played Tegan Jovanka in the BBC television series Doctor Who) on the titles page to become invincible. Name: Dampfmaschine
MemoText: Laden des Programmes: Computer einschalten. ProgrammCassette in den Rekorder legen und an den Anfang vorspulen. Dann am Computer die SHIFT- und gleichzeitig die RUN/STOP-Taste drücken. Jetzt die PLAY-Taste am Rekorder betätigen. Der Programm-Name wird angezeigt - jetzt die RETURN-Taste drücken. Erscheint dann nach ca. 4 Minuten das EUROPA-Zeichen, erneut RETURN drücken und man ist im Programm. Sollte der Ladevorgang beim ersten Mal nicht klappen, bitte noch einmal versuchen. Bitte auch immer die Bedienungs-Anleitung des Computer-Herstellers beachten. Beim ATARI-Programm ist der gesamte Ladevorgang auf Spur 2 mit einer Programm-Musik unterlegt.  Programm-Beschreibung Das Programm simuliert den Lauf einer Dampfmaschine. Bei Spielbeginn wird die Maschine vorbereitet. Per Joystick werden die einzelnen Felder, wie z.B. WASSER, KOHLE, VENTIL oder DYNAMO angewählt und gleichzeitig über die Auslösetaste aktiviert. Wichtig für den Start sind Wasser und Kohle (Menge abhängig von der Dauer des Drückens der Auslösetaste). WASSER - Wasserstandsanzeige im seperaten Feld KOHLE - Mengenanzeige im separaten Feld Danach wird die Maschine über ZÜNDEN angeworfen (C64). Die Temperatur steigt - abhängig von der Mengenrelation Wasser zu Kohle. Bei 100 Grad arbeitet die Maschine - es muß nur noch der Dynamo angeschaltet werden (0 = aus / 1 = an). Schon erscheinen in der Anzeige die ersten Energiepunkte. anz wichtig: Die Druckanzeige muß ständig beobachtet werden. Bei 3 Bar wird es kritisch - der Kessel könnte explodieren! Also schnell das VENTIL öffnen, der Druck fällt und die Dampfmaschine produziert über den Dynamo weitere Energiepunkte. Wasser und Kohle können nachgefüllt werden, bis die Energie-Vorräte am Ende sind. Danach läuft nichts mehr. An der Anzahl der Punkte kann man ablesen, wie gut der Maschinist gearbeitet hat. Sollte der Druck über 3 Bar ansteigen, so explodiert der Kessel und das Spiel ist beendet (C64). Beim ATARI-Spiel dagegen reduzieren sich die Punkte, wenn man im Bereich über 3 Bar ist. Geht nichts mehr, kann sofort ein neues Spiel gestartet werden - Übung macht auch hier den Meister! Name: Desert Fox
MemoText: WHAT WAS FIXED?  While testing Stubenhocker discovered that the northernmost depot in the 'master' scenario sometimes became unreachable, and the game frequently crashed if the player moved around near its location on any level. This was caused by the routine responsible for adding or substracting points depending on the course the player takes through a minefield which occasionally wrote into the internal game map, thereby erasing objects stored there or creating undefined objects causing the crashes. The bug screwed up the scoring within the minefield part, too.  There was also a problem with the rasterirqs during the convoy action part which would sometimes be missed and cause heavy flickering, but some instruction-juggling in the irq-handler should rectify that, at least until the music sets in at the very end of the part.  Finally, the game was apparently meant to be restartable via reset-button (thanks to TheRyk for telling me about the reset-behaviour btw, as my breadbin's reset circuit ignores any CBM80-stuff), but since the various io-ports weren't initialized after reset the game couldn't set the proper VIC-bank or memory configuration then.   WHAT ELSE WAS CHANGED?  Scoring can now go up to 999,999 instead of just 99,999, what was not enough for the 'grandmaster'-level.  An option to replace 'Ambush' radio messages with static to add an element of surprise to the game.  Two previously unused samples can be included into the gameplay (optionally, because they can introduce additional flickering during the action parts and some people might prefer the game without that):  - 'Mayday' will sound if your tank amasses critical damage.  - 'Achtung' will play whenever you are on the map screen and one of the    allied depots has less than 9 hours left until the nazis take it. As a    bonus, the zoom box will be placed on that depot so that you'll    instantly know which depot is in danger.  Original look or swastika-free replacement graphics can be selected.  The letter '1' was changed to look more like '1' and less like ']'.  The game will automatically pause while zooming in on a depot so one can carefully check its stats without losing game time or having to hit space every time. You can still manually pause the game via spacebar in other situations.  After you won or lost a game you can now move joystick #2 down to restart instead of hitting restore, what might be useful for DTV-users. Why down instead of fire? Because the firebutton is required for the depot zoom function, which remains functional after losing to allow to check all depots in order to refine your strategy for the next attempt. Restore can still be used to abort a game in progress at almost any time (except when the sample-player temporarily steals the nmi vector).    HOW DO I PLAY THIS GAME?  Read the manual :-) No really, the game even offers practice modes and is almost self-explanatory, except for a few things:  To hit something with the tank gun the target must be under the crosshair when the shell arrives. Luckily you don't have to shoot with perfect deflection as you can also steer the shells while they are underway by turning the gun (don't complain about the lack of realism just yet, wait at least until you've seen the turbo-charged Tiger tanks :-)).  Before you can move your tank over the map, you have to use the radio icon to set the direction. This will also inform you of any enemies that are ahead in the chosen direction.  If you can't reach a depot before its time runs out (which is your main objective, by the way) you can use the airstrike icon to vector some Spitfires to its location. If they arrive before it's too late the depot's survival time is increased by 30 hours of game time. This can be done only once per game.  You could also seek a convoy action sequence, where you have to shoot a difficulty level dependant number of planes to win (each red plane is worth 100 points, each green one will cost you 300 points, so don't shoot those!):  5000 - Challenger 5200 - Crusader 5400 - Strategy 5600 - Master 5800 - Grand Master  If you get enough points the depot you previously selected via the zoom-icon on the map will receive additional supplies and thus last longer. This can be done as often as you want.  Should you beat rommel (the red cross/swastika on the map that starts to hunt you after a while), one depot will be automatically saved (usually the depot that had the most time left).   WHAT'S ROMMEL'S REVENGE MODE HOTKEY GOOD FOR?  It's just a shortcut to launch the game after disabling all trainers, enabling the sneaky ambush and extrasample option, setting Rommel's strength to 10 and the mine repair factor to 1. Those are Stubenhocker's preferred settings, you know :-)

Name: Exile
MemoText: 1) Fly to the right until you see a grenade on the ground (it looks like a little grey ball with a dot in the middle), use the '<' Key to pick up the grenade.   2) Fly to the right, go under the big spaceship and go down the pit/hole in the ground. You will now be at a door, which is built into the floor below your feet. Stand to the left of the door, use the '>' key to throw the grenade. The door will explode and you go inside , down the tunnel. (Remember to press the 'R' key 6 times so if you die you will start at the location you pressed 'R', instead of starting way back at the start.)   3) A little 4 legged creature is blocking the path, (press runstop to crawl / fly horizontally), push the creature out the way, it will fall off the edge and hit the ground and explode. Go down and then up the passage to the left where you find the Icer (Gun) lying on the floor. Use '<' to pick it up, press '1' to activate the gun.   4) Go down the tunnel and go into the first room on your left (by the way, when you enter this room 4 or 5 energy balls will make a buzzing sound and fly towards you, you will need to shoot these.) In this room, fly to the top centre of the room. In the pit/room above you, you should see a Blue object sitting on the floor. (Blue key) CONGRATULATIONS...

It shows 'The Games: Bummer Edition' loading screen including a dragon and 14 pictures of team behind the game and a scrolltext and music.  To view it in the tape version you must load the tape as usual until you arrive in the menu. Choose 'Opening Ceremonies', then the game will ask you to rewind tape, BUT don't do that, just press the fire button. Wait until the counter goes up to around 320 and the screen starts flashing until the counter stops at 340.   To view it in the disk version you must load the game as usual until you arrive in the menu. Choose 'Change Names', enter the same name for each of the 8 players and press F7 afterwards. Select 'Return to Village' and press the button again to return to the menu. Now the second menu option offers you to 'Display Easter Egg'.

MemoText: Bug or programming fault (TESTED ON THE G64 AND TAP VERSIONS): When you enter a certain area within the first level the screen scrolls up and you're able to kill the enemies inside. When you leave the area afterwards the screen scrolls down only a bit. Now the player is caught in this area because he can't move left or right to walk around it. ------------------------------------------------------------------- (see Bug Report in extras) you can walk left and right you just have to be standing in line with the bottom of the barrier and you must be pixel perfect. (it will look like you are walking through the barrier) but unless you destroy the purple barriers (XX) *first* you will get trapped at the point shown in the picture (2) for the same scroll down reason.  I do not think this is a bug, but an actual part of the game. to remember the layout of the level and avoid getting trapped. e.g. level 2 also has an area where you can get trapped. with an invicible wall in front of you and no scroll down.  I have managed to load level 2 sucessfully on the G64 version but the disk level loader is very unreliable and works only 40% of the time. (thats only if you don't breathe on the keyboard or blink by accident) which is a pain in the neck because after every game over level 1 reloads. (or should i say tries to reload) and you have to start the game all over again. more work seems to have gone into the disk protection rather than function.  no one could have ever play tested it!  for the best level loading results (99%) use the Tape Version. tested all levels to final end screen.  approx tape counter in vice level 1 000 level 2 033 level 3 066 level 4 092 level 5 128  INFO (not a BUG) when you lose your 5 lives, even after loading a new level 2-3-4-5 you will find the soilder stuck on that level unable to move. The only possible way to continue is to press RESTORE. which will reload level 1.  bugs!! Name: Reaxion
MemoText: Deep in the heart of the hills of Wenley something is amiss. The Wenley Moor nuclear power plant, buried five hundred feet below ground level, is at risk. The control computer has been infected by a virus from an unknown source. This virus has caused the complete shutdown of all computer systems and a total randomisation of the core settings. Fortunately, the computer is now offline, but there's a catch; all thirty cores are now dangerously unstable and, although all shields are in place for now, they will soon be unable to contain the entropy. It's up to you to straighten this mess out.  You have at your disposal a core monitor unit to remotely edit the rod statuses of each core in turn, but here's the problem; when you toggle a rod a chain reaction occurs in the surrounding eight causing them to flip states too. And worse still, the shielding has to be disabled to allow the monitor unit access to a core, effectively giving each a time limit until meltdown. Succeed and you save the entire planet from a gigantic nuclear explosion. Fail and that's it...  Control the monitor unit with a joystick in port 2, directions move the unit around over the fifty six rods of each core and fire toggles states.  Review: 'Go on, give it a try... but don't send the receipts for the hair replacement therapy.' Commodore Format  Trivia: To get infinite time, simply type 'silicon graphics' on the titles page. Wenley Moor is a Doctor Who reference, from the story 'The Silurians'.

Name: Rock Run
MemoText: When your warp drive kicks out in a desolate and totally uninhabited part of the universe, you find yourself somewhat stuck. After fashioning repairs, at least enough to get you home, and set off to accelerate back up to make the jump to warp, only to find an asteroid belt in your way!  The repairs you've made are ad-hoc, you get one shot at warping and that's it; so you must navigate through the asteroids as the engines wind up to warp speed. Control your ship using a joystick in port 2.  Trivia: this is actually Rock Run V2, with the original using expanded sprites for the rocks. Tony was a serious addict of the original and a special 'nightmare' edition exists of the original which starts at the hardest difficulty level.

Name: Star Trek - The Adventure
MemoText: The second version included is a reconstruction without graphics. For some reason the verbs, nouns, adverbs and objects had been removed from the code. Using the messages and the puzzles I was able to reconstruct the game into a playable version. I did not change any puzzles or text. Although I think some things could have been better. For instance there is a button in the game, but you can't press it. You have to do something less common. I did remove some bugs like being able to find the same object over and over again by adding some markers to the code, correcting  the wrong message at a certain puzzle and a few minor other things. It is quite a difficult game to solve due to some farfetched commands, but this is how it was written by the author.   This version is without the graphics and hopefully they can be added to a later version (work on progress by someone else).   Anyway I hope you will enjoy it.

Name: Beauty and the Beast [Preview]
MemoText: My name is Maham Samanpajouh producer of Beauty and the Beast in 1996 for Commodore 64. Thank you for your review on the GTW64. As the programmer and project director of this game, I have to say; I had only 16 years old when I finished the game. The original game was on Tape, which I do not know if you had it before or not. (I attached it for your reference).  Since I worked hard those days in order to finish the game, I would be glad if you could consider the followings into your review too.      We used music of different artists, because nobody was expert that time on creating sounds and music for C64. Furthermore, there was not any Software for composing tracks on C64 as well.     Me and Reza tried so hard to daub lots of the graphics for the game ourselves. I didn?t use the Last Ninja engine at all. I develop a basic compression method instead of Last Ninja Level Mapping Engine and this is the reason we don?t have more than 6-7 screens per level. This is while Last Ninja game normally has more than 20 screens per level.     I developed the tape loader from scratch. It looks a lot like Last Ninja Cyberload Loaders but it is not. I?m sure Tape experts can proof this is a new loader and identify this as well since it is a new loader.     The game totally has Developers Introduction, Initial Demo, 3 Different levels (Village, The Wood and The Castle) and a Final Demo. The game end is accessible by normal play.     There may be many bugs inside the game because this game never tested by other people except us.     We started to develop an other game named ??Mountain Combaters? after Beauty and The Beast but the game never completed because it was too late. Basically, the game was ISOMETRIC like LN series and It was technically more advance than Beauty and The Beast. I manage to use raster techniques a lot and a level graphics engine like LN. Some Screenshots and an Initial Intro is available.     We never published the game, we did not earn a penny and no one appreciated us for creating such game. Those days are gone now but one thing is still true that we do love C64 forever.     My final sad words is Reza Shamsian who was my long-term school friend and involved with Storyboard and Graphics of both games is not with us anymore. He passed away 5 years ago because of a sudden Heart Attack when he was only 27. God bless him.  I hope I could give some comments about the only game, which was developed in Iran for Commodore 64 in 1996.

MemoText: Expeditions Copyright © 1984 MECC  MECC stands for Minnesota Educational Computing Corporation. Expeditions is a suite of three educational text games: Furs, Voyageur, and Oregon. In Furs, the player takes the role of an Ottawa Indian leading a fur-trading expedition across three routes in North America in the 1600's. In Voyageur, the player travels into fur trading country in North America between 1770 and 1830. Oregon is a simulated journey across the Oregon Trail from Independence, Missouri to Oregon City. The player is leading a family of five across the New Frontier with all the perils it brings.  MECC would later take the concept of 'Oregon' and turn it into its own educational game to run on DOS-based PCs, Macintosh, Windows 3.1x, and even Windows 9x. MECC would call this educational game 'The Oregon Trail.' It would be utilized by educational institutes and home computers and would eventually be purchased from MECC by Softkey and The Learning Channel.  Expeditions is the birthplace of The Oregon Trail and now a part of software history.

Name: Tapeworm
MemoText: Author's note: -------------- Although part of a multi-part demo I did, I decided to give Tape Worm a separate entry as its a game.  Whilst doing the Am I Dead Yet demo, I for some reason decided it would be a good idea to do a mini-game as one of the parts and knocked out this very simple Silkworm clone in SEUCK within about half a day.  There is practically no background graphics or level data in it at all.  As a result, the end result is very rough and unplayable.  It is more like something that has been created in Game Creator than SEUCK.   The clear inspiration was Silverfish by Alf Yngve, which had been released a year before by Psytronik.  Alf did things properly and gave a real sense of illusion that the game scrolled sideways.  I didn't really hit the spot with this one, with the flying trees looking like tree bullets.  To be honest, it was a piss take - hence the silly name to reference Silkworm.

Name: Wilder Westen
MemoText: Laden des Programmes: Computer einschalten. ProgrammCassette in den Rekorder legen und an den Anfang vorspulen. Dann am Computer die Shift- und gleichzeitig die RUN/STOP-Taste drücken. Dann die Play-Taste am Rekorder drücken. Das Programm wird nun automatisch geladen.  Programm-Beschreibung Action ist in WILDER WESTEN angesagt - und eine große Portion an Geschicklichkeit. Denn mit dem Colt - er wird über den Steuerknüppel bewegt - muß auf die unterschiedlichsten Gegenstände geziehlt und geballert werden. Das übrigens geschieht mit der Auslösetaste am Steuerknüppel. 20 Schüsse sind im Magazin und für jeden getroffenen Gegenstand gibt es Punkte. Doch wehe man trifft aus Versehen die kleine Bombe - dann wird das Spiel recht abrupt vorzeitig beendet. In diesem Spiel kann abwechselnd gespielt werden - wer erreicht die meisten Punkte? Der Höchststand wird übrigens auf dem Bildschirm angezeigt.  Viel Spaß und Action- und wenn die Experten unter sich sind, kann auch gegen die Uhr gespielt werden. Einfach mal probieren!  Ein Heimcomputer-Spiel aus dem EUROPA Computer-Club (C) 1984 MILLER INTERNATIONAL Schallplatten GmbH, 2085 Quickborn bei Hamburg

MemoText: SHOGOTH is a two-sided disk text ('Infocom-like') adventure in Italian. It received a Gold Medal award on the Italian edition of the monthly magazine Zzap! and it was produced by D.W. SOFTWARE and distributed by SYSTEMS EDITORIALE. The reason for which it is very rare is hilariously dramatic: part of the disk archives of Systems Editoriale was inadvertently marked as 'Junk' and destroyed in the course of a plant relocation, just before the game went into production. Guess where all the masters and backup were stored. In the meantime, the final copy given to the editorial offices of Zzap! simply was taken home by a never-to-be-found contributor, while the only work copy of the game left in the hands of the authors was a copy-protected autoplay version, with the possibility of typing commands eradicated from the code. Yet the game was finished, very good (same quality of 'Brimstone, dream of Gawain', if you are an adventure freak) and a few preproduction copies are known to exists somewhere.  And, in case you're wondering how do I know of this all: I was the author of the text portion of the game and second game designer. You can trust me on this.  Fabio Rossi

MemoText: Author's note: -------------- I was a huge fan of Thing on a Spring and the character in general, and hence I was inspired to produce a comic strip (which i'll find and scan some day!) and also a new game done in SEUCK!  I can't say that the theme was kept very close to the original game - which was more of a cutesy affair.  Thing was now thrown deep into Russia and was doing war against an army, and carried a machine gun!  But then I was 11 at the time, and a game with guns was the way to go!  I managed to get the usual road graphics down, some flat buildings and simple enemies to shoot.  Thing was a very basic animating character as well, and turned into dog tags when shot.  Some of the more interesting parts were the underground tunnel, and the finale on a moving truck going sideways ... which was borrowed from Cops by Alf Yngve, which was probably my favourite SEUCK game of all time and one of the rare SEUCK titles I will load up periodically to go through.  It never progressed further beyond this point as I got bored of it quickly and moved onto other projects.  The game again was written over the top of Outlaw, and parts of that game get blended in periodically in places where i've been lazy.   Also, the second player is the character from Cute Land... and the reason I think is because I wrote Cute Land eventually over the top of Thing On a Spring and saved it on another tape.   I probably just started drawing the sprites and realised I needed to save Thing again,  then did some more work to turn it into Cute Land, and save it as that game on another tape.  Anyway ... nothing special at all, and just a fond development memory of mine.

Name: Synetic
MemoText: Author's note: -------------- Synetic was my last ever SEUCK title released, and also the best too.  It was started in 1997 and inspired by various games such as Alien Breed and also Alien Smash which Commodore Format had on their Power Pack.  I worked on the game on and off for a few years,  mostly having a break due to GCSE exams in 1998.  The idea was to try and combine several different game play styles into a single load.  I wanted the Alien Breed style level, a sideways platforms and ladders level, a 3D perspective top down level,  a Sideways scroller and a Space Shooter all in one.  It was to be the most ambitious title I had done in the SEUCK engine, and as a result I didn't want to rush it.  I got to a point where the game was pretty much complete and over time I just kept making small tweaks to it.  Most of the actual game work was complete back in 1997, which included a full intro sequence like I had done previously with Xavier and SGA 2.  Again, the intro was to be my most ambitious yet - and included some neat features such as a zooming planet and a crash landing sequence.  There is also a part where the first part of the game plays out before the credits roll.  So things got stuck for a while - the plan was to stick things potentially on Commodore Zone's cover mount, and I tinkered with various music combinations in the game during this time.  I was keen on a lot of JCH's tunes, and XRay was my favourite for the intro. However, the mixing of the sideways scrolling and space ship parts on Synetic didn't quite fit together neatly and I was struggling.  The game needed some enhancements to really make it slick, and so I asked Jon Wells if he could enhance it.  Jon thankfully agreed, though he got caught up for a bit - and after discussing back in 1998 and producing some stunning tunes, things went quiet.  Then finally I got Jon to start kicking things off in 2000.  He got me to produce a logo and font for the title screen, and had the idea of having little text screens between scenes.  He also encouraged creating a end sequence, which he could password protect.  Building on from the intro, I aimed to produce the best possible ending I had ever done - and managed to get something which hopefully rewarded the player.  Vinny Mainolfi recently awarded it 10/10 on his C64endings.co.uk website.  Jon's enhancements really made the game click, and it made a very good impression.  It also just made the very last issue of Commodore Zone and its covermount, so hopefully got a bit of extra exposure.  I'm very very proud of the game overall, as I feel that it combines all of what I learnt from when I started in 1993 and progressed with during my time with the tool.  At this stage though I had felt I had done enough with the tool and it was time to move on.  I did briefly toy with finishing Sensation, but shortly after decided to cancel all my projects and concentrate on college and uni work.  It wasn't until Sub Hunter in 2004 when I started doing games again.  Whilst archiving all my work disks, I found many different varients of Synetic from over the course of its development lifetime.  I have placed all of these onto the disks in this folder.  Some versions have very slight differences in terms of title screens, life counter styles and also a different screen where the player turns into a ship.    I also found an alternate version of a Synetic title screen which was produced by Richard Bayliss.  At one stage I thought that Jon was not going to get chance to do the Synetic enhancements, so Richard stepped in to help and produced some mockup titles and instructions.  I found these recently which were unused, and followed the instructions to create a build with the titles in place.    No loading screen was ever done, but I did find a loader screen quick sketch on some paper recently and that has been scanned and added too.

Name: Computer-Kran!
MemoText: Laden des Programmes: Computer einschalten. Programm-Cassette in den Rekorder legen und an den Anfang vorspulen. Dann am Computer die SHIFT- und gleichzeitig die RUN/STOP-Taste drücken. Jetzt die PLAY-Taste am Rekorder betätigen. Der Programm-Name wird angezeigt - jetzt die RETURN-Taste drücken. Weitere Ladeanweisung des Computers beachten! Die Ladezeit beträgt ca. 4 Minuten. Sollte der Ladevorgang beim ersten Mal nicht klappen, bitte noch einmal versuchen. Bitte auch immer die Bedienungs-Anleitung des Computer-Herstellers beachten. Beim ATARI-Programm ist der gesamte Ladevorgang auf Spur 2 mit einer Programm-Musik unterlegt.  Programm-Beschreibung Als Kranführer steuern Sie einen vollprogrammierbaren Kran. Befehl für Befehl wird eingegeben mit dem Ziel, die immer an einem anderen Ort aufgestellte Kiste mit möglichst wenigen und genauen Befehlen anzugeben. Dazu werden Kran und Laufkatze genau über die Kiste gebracht, der Greifer wird abgesenkt und dann wird die Kiste gegriffen. Die Form für die Befehlseingabe: BEFEHL (Leerzeichen) WERT (max. 99). Es müssen nach eigener Einschätzung Werte zwischen 0 und 99 eingegeben werden. Der Kran nimmt nur folgende Befehle an: VOR - bewegt Kran nach links ZURÜCK - bewegt Kran nach rechts RECHTS - Katze runter/rechts LINKS - Katze hoch/links HOCH - hebt Greifer RUNTER - senkt Greifer. Der letzte Befehl lautet GREIFEN 0. Der Cursor kann über die DEL-Taste nach links gebracht werden. Einmal eingegebene Befehle werden mit RETURN abgeschlossen und können dann weder gelöscht noch geändert werden. Jeder Befehl kostet wertvolles Benzin - das ist wichtig für die Gesamtbewertung Deiner Steuerung am Spielende.  Von der C64-Version abweichende Programm-Beschreibung ATARI: Hinweise zeigt das Programm. START über TAB und neues Spiel über CLEAR. Im Teil KRAN VON VORNE erscheint die Kiste erst dann, wenn die Laufkatze g e n a u über der Kiste positioniert ist. Der letzte Befehl lautet GREIFEN 1. Und nun viel Spaß und Unterhaltung mit dem Computer-Kran!

Fortunately, the computer is now offline, but there's a catch; all ninety nine cores are now dangerously unstable and, although all shields are in place for now, they will soon be unable to contain the entropy. It's up to you to straighten this mess out.  You have at your disposal a core monitor unit to remotely edit the rod statuses of each core in turn, but here's the problem; when you toggle a rod a chain reaction occurs in the surrounding eight causing them to flip states too. And worse still, the shielding has to be disabled to allow the monitor unit access to a core, effectively giving each a time limit until meltdown. Succeed and you save the entire planet from a gigantic nuclear explosion. Fail and that's it...  Control the monitor unit with a joystick in port 2, directions move the unit around over the fifty six rods of each core and fire toggles states. Press runstop to pause.  This is a total re-coding (as well as featuring a large amount of new graphics and a new soundtrack!) of the original Reaxion and now includes the extra sixty nine levels from the Amiga conversion designed and coded by Sean.  Trivia: Wenley Moor is still a Doctor Who reference taken from the story 'The Silurians'. The archive was revised 9th January 2006 to correct a bug in the highscore table code.

MemoText: Laden des Programmes: Computer einschalten. Programm-Cassette in den Rekorder legen und an den Anfang vorspulen. Dann am Computer die SHIFT- und gleichzeitig die RUN/STOP-Taste drücken. Jetzt die PLAY-Taste am Rekorder betätigen. Der Programm-Name wird angezeigt - jetzt die RETURN-Taste drücken. Erscheint dann nach ca. 4 Minuten das EUROPA-Zeichen, erneut RETURN drücken und man ist im Programm. Sollte der Ladevorgang beim ersten Mal nicht klappen, bitte noch einmal versuchen. Bitte auch immer die Bedienungs-Anleitung des Computer-Herstellers beachten. Beim ATARI-Programm ist der gesamte Ladevorgang auf Spur 2 mit einer Programm-Musik unterlegt.  Programm-Beschreibung Auf dem Spielfeld wird neben der Hauptstraße nach Gold gegraben, das dann zur Bank gebracht werden muß. Das Spiel beginnt, nachdem eine 6 gewürfelt wurde. Das Würfeln übernimmt für das ganze Spiel der Computer. Bevor es vorangeht, muß nach auf Feld A eingekauft werden: die Verpflegung durch Eingabe einer Zahl von 1-9. Merke: je höher die Zahl, desto größer die Verpflegung und damit längeres Durchhalten auf dem langen Trail - aber auch langsameres Vorankommen. Denn man muß auch noch noch Gold suchen und dieses aufnehmen. Die Zusatz-Ausrüstung mit Werkzeug wird durch Eingabe einer 0 oder 1 = ja oder nein eingegeben. Merke: ohne diese Ausrüstung können Unterbrechungen auf der Straße nicht überwunden werden. Nach Gold kann man wahlweise auf beiden Seiten der Wegstrecke graben (bei Atari nur nicht auf den freien, hellen Feldern). Das Vorankommen des Spielers wird durch das Würfeln des Computers bestimmt. Beim Graben findet der Spieler Gold oder eine Kiste, ebenfalls mit Gold oder aber mit einem Ereignis (Giftschlange, Räuber). Gesammelte Goldstücke werden dem Punktekonto zugeschrieben. Sicher sind diese Funde erst in der Bank (auf dem Feld B). Dieses Feld kann zum Einlösen nur direkt erreicht werden - sonst geht es minder zurück. Unterbrechungen auf der Straße können nur mit der Zusatzausrüstung überwunden werden. Spiel-Ende ist, wenn Spieler verhungert sind oder überall gegraben werde. Gespielt wird über Joystick und Auslösetaste.  Hinweise: Je mehr ein Spieler trägt (Gold, Verpflegung, Ausrüstung), um so langsamer kommt dieser voran. Wird bei zwei Spielern das gegnerische Feld direkt erreicht so wird dieser gefangen und man bekommt sein Gold. Es kann in beide Richtungen gelaufen werden. So - und nun viel Spaß. Wir empfehlen, vor dem Spiel die richtige Ausrüstung zusammenzustellen und erst dann auf die Goldsuche zu gehen.  Ein Heimcomputer-Spiel aus dem EUROPA Computer-Club © 1985 MILLER INTERNATIONAL Schallplatten GmbH, 2085 Ouickborn bei Hamburg

Die Zahlen lassen sich horizontal und vertikal per Computerhand (C64) oder Pfeil (Atari) über das Freifeld verschieben. Computerhand oder Pfeil per Joystick auf die zu verschiebende Zahl bewegen und durch Druck auf die Auslösetaste bestätigen. Ziel ist es, mit möglichst wenigen Zügen die neben dem Spielfeld abgebildete Lösung zu erreichen. Hinweis für ATARI: Über SELECT können 3 Schwierigkeitsstufen angewählt werden. Name: Rasen-Mäher
MemoText: Laden des Programmes: Computer einschalten. ProgrammCassette in den Rekorder legen und an den Anfang vorspulen. Dann am Computer die Shift- und gleichzeitig die RUN/STOP-Taste drücken. Dann die Play-Taste am Rekorder drücken. Das Programm wird nun automatisch geladen.  Programm-Beschreibung: In möglichst kurzer Zeit soll der Rasen gemäht werden. Doch viele Hindernisse machen den Umgang mit dem Gerät - besonders wenn der Schnellgang eingeschaltet ist - zu einem recht schwierigen Erlebnis. 1. Auswahl der 5 unterschiedlichen Gärten: Joystick nach oben oder unten drücken 2. Spiel-Start Auslöseknopf drücken - der Rasenmäher wird in die Ausgangsposition gesetzt. Erneutes Drücken des Auslöseknopfes dann für Spielbeginn. 3. Ändern der Geschwindigkeit Während der Fahrt mit dem Rasenmäher den Auslöseknopf drücken und dann Joystick nach oben - schnellere Fahrt Joystick nach unten - langsamere Fahrt Wichtig: Während der Geschwindigkeitsveränderung kann nicht gelenkt werden. Zum Weiterfahren einfach den Joystick in die Mittelstellung bringen und den Auslöseknopf loslassen. Natürlich darf nur auf dem Rasen gefahren werden - und beim Überfahren von schon gemähtem Rasen gibt es einen entsprechenden Punktabzug. Ist das Werk vollbracht geht es automatisch in den nächsten Garten. Das Spiel wird beendet wenn keiner der fünf Rasenmäher mehr zur Verfügung steht. Viel Spaß und Unterhaltung - und möglichst wenig Hindernisse beim Rasenmähen. Touch
MemoText: Laden des Programmes: Computer einschalten. Programm-Cassette in den Rekorder legen und an den Anfang vorspulen. Dann am Computer die SHIFT- und gleichzeitig die RUN/STOP-Taste drücken. Jetzt die PLAY-Taste am Rekorder betätigen. Der Programm-Name wird angezeigt jetzt die RETURN-Taste drücken. Erscheint dann nach ca. 3 Minuten dos EUROPA-Zeichen, erneut RETURN drücken und man ist im Programm. Sollte der Ladevorgang heim ersten Mal nicht klappen, bitte noch einmal versuchen. Bitte auch immer die Bedienungs-Anleitung des Computer-Herstellers beachten. Beim ATARI-Programm ist der gesamte Ladevorgang auf Spur 2 mit einer Programm-Musik unterlegt.  Programm- Beschreibung Bei diesem Spiel kommt es auf das eigene Gedächtnis an. Der Computer läßt farbige Felder in unterschiedlicher Reihenfolge aufleuchten, die dann in der richtigen Reihenfolge nachzuspielen sind. Das geschieht, indem ein Zeichen (Hand bei C64) mittels Joystick auf das Feld gebracht und die Auslösetaste gedrückt wird. Bei ATARI wird der Joystick (jeweils in Richtung der aufgeleuchteten Farbfelder) diagonal gedrückt wird. Die Anzahl der Felder nimmt von Stufe zu Stufe zu und die jeweiligen Pausen werden kürzer. Bei einem Fehler scheidet der Spieler aus. Achtung: bei zu langer Überlegungszeit ertönt ebenfalls ein Signal - zum Ausscheiden. Name: 64 Sub Hunt
MemoText: You're in command of a Destroyer locked in battle with an Enemy Submarine. The sub's commander is aware of your presence and is taking evasive action. As the sub unpredictably changes course, you attempt to hit it with your Depth Charges. Drop a depth charge by pressing any key as your ship passes over the sub. Each time you hit the sub, he's forced closer and closer to the surface. The game ends when he has been forced all the way up, and you pull alongside and board him. It's not easy to hit the submarine, but since you have an unlimited supply of depth charges, his surrender is just a matter of time. A clock is provided so you can keep track of your times in different battles. All hands, man your battle stations! And have fun playing Sub Hunt.

Name: Gravity III - The Final Rescue
MemoText: The last ever game in the Gravity series, featuring much nicer graphics, with special thanks to Zeitgeist/Civitas. Your mission is to pick up medical cargo from the delivery ship above Planet Zerox. Then deliver the cargo to the Lunar HQ, by landing on the landing pad. Unfortunately your mission will be quite a tough one, as an evil alien empire knew about your delivery. So they decided to send a load of their assorted alien ships to guard the planet and smash into you. While you are landing your space craft, make sure you avoid collision with the alien ships, otherwise you could lose a life. This game was entered for the game compo at the Vision 2003 Party, and won the competition - as there were no other Commodore 64 entries for this compo. :o)  /MUSICIANS/B/Bayliss_Richard/Super_Galaxys_Title_Music.sid (title screen) /MUSICIANS/B/Bayliss_Richard/Brain_Smasher.sid (in-game)

Name: Anger
MemoText: Back in 1991, I was toying around a little with the Shoot Em Up Construction Kit and a few years back, I have been lucky enough to find some old games of mine on some tapes back in the days.  Probably in 1991, I wondered to myself if it was possible to do a kind of breakout style game, using the Shoot Em Up Construction Kit. Unfortunately, the game did not turn out as is was meant to have been. It was most definitely complete and utterly a load of pants. Whoever thought that breakout is possible with SEUCK must think again. Maybe possible with SEUCK Redux though, but what's the point with this game?  You play a paddle, which shoots a ball at the walls moving towards you. You only get one life, but if you get enough bricks, an extra life is awarded. Sadly this game is virtually impossible to play.

Send your answers on a postcard. :o)  Oh, by the way, if you are really looking forward to playing this game, then be prepared for an incredible experience of major disappointment, because this game is even worse than a badly cooked dinner.

Name: Great Giana Sisters II, The
MemoText: This is NOT a simple hack of Giana-Sisters 1 which has new Stages only. The Seven-A-Three has completely reprogrammed many parts of the Game and also removed some Bugs from Giana I.  CHANGES FROM GIANA I to GIANA II: - 40 totally new Stages with very different Gameplay (instead of 33 Stages which play more similar)  - Secrets to find out in nearly every Stage - 2 Secret Stages (find the right Warps) - 10 Treasuries (instead of only 5 in Giana I) - New Sprite-Control-Program (was a huge Part in the Program, done by Chrille). That means:   - Giana can jump on moving plattforms (Elevators)   - Giana can swim in water   - Giana can fly by collecting the Jet-Pack-Extra   - Treasure-Chests which contain the same extras like the extra-blocks but Giana can collect them without jumping under a block   - 19 new small enemies (some of them must be shot 2 or 3 times to kill them)   - Some enemies can follow Giana   - Jumping enemies fall down when they loose the ground and bounce against the ceiling when there is not enough space.   - Some jumping enemies can also jump to the left and to the right   - Enemies also appear in the first screen (in Giana 1 they had to scroll in)    - 4 new big enemies (End-Monsters)   - The Dragon spits fire now   - You'll get thousands of points when you kill an end-monster (instead of nothing :-( in Giana I)   - Softer collision-detection with monsters    - Issue (Bug) cleared : Giana won't die anymore BEFORE she touches an enemy   - Replaced the annoying fast bug/turtle/mouse(whatever) with a real monster so Gianas Bullet cannot be caught by that monster   - The exit-elevator has the right look now (not in Multi-Color)   - The Bomb-Extra kills all small monsters now (also like worms or balls) and not only the ones who can also be shot (Who needs a Bomb when you just as well can shoot the same enemies). But this won't work for End-Monsters (This would be almost too easy). - New Stage-Initialisation-Program (done by Merlin) That means:   - You are able to train a special stage that you already have played, even without using a cheat   - Stages after Stage 14 will be loaded from Disk, the new Endmonsters do the same   - Timelimit can be set different for each Stage between 1 and 1000 seconds   - Warps do not simply teleport Giana 3 Stages foreward but also less or more   - Diamonds (and some other objects) have different colours in different Stages   - In the 'Heaven-Stage' Giana can walk on clouds - Faster and shorter scroll-routine (by Merlin) - Also fixed an issue (bug) in the scroll-routine that made Giana slip from an edge when she just landed on it while scrolling - New Stage-Build-up-Routine (by Merlin) - New Objekts like new walls or upside down turned peaks - Giana cannot 'cheat' anymore by standing on the red peaks - hidden corridors and invisible bridges (in later Stages only) - some hidden extras and bonus - start with 5 Lives instead of 3 - You can always view the high-score-list by pressing 'H' in the Title-Screen - Also used the hidden Song of Giana-Sisters (first time in Stage 17) - and last but not least: An animated End-Sequence, and a nice Intro with many informations and hints

Name: Super Seven
MemoText: This was one of my brave attempts at making my own puzzle game. A kind of tetris, but with a difference. Sadly today, I find my Super Seven to be not so super :o(  The aim of this game is to drop a dice on top of one of the dices that is in the bottom of the container. Each dice switches it's value, and your job is to simply match the value of your dice to one of the dices at the bottom of the screen. If you mess up, then a life will be lost. Once all lives are lost, it is game over. Simple gameplay, but rather boring I have to agree about.

Name: Super Pac Twins
MemoText: This was originally an unfinished game, which was released on to the Commodore Format cover tape, and was lacking a front end, and picture. In 2002, I asked the game's author if I could update his game by adding a front end and some other additional pieces of code. Although I was still sort of a beginner at programming in assembly language. The result turned out quite good at the end.  Play the role of a green or a yellow pac ball around the maze, chomping those blue pellets. There are also pellets of a different colour, which will enhance game play. Watch out for those boulders before they drain your energy and squash you. There are 100 (or maybe more) levels for you to pit you skills against before you are able to complete this game.

Name: Kids Say the Darndest Things... to Computers
Warpzone Remix
MemoText: Warpzone is a small Robotron-inspired shoot'em-up that was written for Commodore Zone issue 16's coverdisk in 2001. The original version was finished something like two hours before the disk was due to be mastered so the levels in that game were quite unfair and hadn't been playtested properly.  After the original game was mentioned on the message board at Lemon 64 during a conversation about Robotron variants on the C64, 4-Mat dug out his source and put an improved set of levels together as well as making a few other tweaks to the source including a new two joystick support feature. The game still suffers a little from slow-down, but when the screen gets that busy it's a blessing in disguise!  Review: 'Judging from the screenshot i didn't think i would have like it, but the game-highscore screen kinda got some oldskool feelinx up in me :) (which doesn't happen often) Much like old scenish games or something. And... the music is f**king cool!' Cyberbrain/Noname, from the C64 Scene Database

MemoText: Improvements according to listing: ---------------------------------- line 10-changed 2nd POKE to 53280 to change border color. line 330-modified so Z$(4) is the beginning of the variable. Was Z$(4)=z$(4)+ line 540-changed Y$(3) to Y$(2)  When time left ticks down to 99 seconds, an extra digit is added both to the time left & punters left. 0 onto the time (basically 3rd digit still present on screen. I think its weird for cars & ducks to occupy the same line, but thats the way the listing is written.

(left arrow) is used to quit the game and it does so by using the STOP command (break). so if you move joystick in port 1, you could accidently stop the game. this is infact the problem with PORT 1 not the game.  i have de-compiled the BASIC and changed a few lines so now it pauses the game and waits for another key press to QUIT (J or N) and all STOP commands have been removed or replaced with the END command.  also fixed a small bug.. the '-' cursor no longer eats the score graphics.

Name: Kikstart C16
MemoText: 'Experience all the excitement of dirt bike riding in this real life simulation. Push your bike to it's limits as you jump over logs and other obstacles. It's a race against the clock as your time is limited for each course. Test your skills as a biker on 16 different courses in this action simulation. Joystick in port 2. Fire button to jump.'  This game was re-sourced from the Commodore 16 original by Shaun Southern, converted to the Commodore 64 and then optimised before being bugfixed (re-timed for the slower machine, scroll routine optimised, data corruption on the final level repaired, occasional glitches in the scrolling at top speed fixed). But why did we convert this game when the C64 already has the original Kikstart you might ask? Because Kikstart for the C16 is a very different game, a single player race against the clock rather than the split screen competition of the C64 and great fun to play - fun that C64 gamers have missed out on for all of these years! But now here it is, running in an almost identical form on the C64 apart from some cosmetic modifications and a shiny new hardware sprite for the bike - enjoy!  Review: 'Fans of the original motocross classic will love it, and for those new to the game (like me) playing Kikstart proves to be an enjoyable (yet equally frustrating) experience.' James Monkman, RGCD  Trivia: This conversion is so close that even the original cheat mode activation still works correctly! Along with an all-new Cosine 'crack' intro (well, technically this is a crack... in a fairly vague sort of way), the game is included with full documentation taken from the C16 cassette inlay.

Name: Octopus
MemoText: Laden des Programmes: Computer einschalten. ProgrammCassette in den Rekorder legen und an den Anfang vorspulen. Dann am Computer die Shift- und gleichzeitig die RUN/STOPTaste drücken. Jetzt die Play-Taste am Rekorder drücken. Erscheint das EUROPA-Zeichen, RETURN drücken und man ist im Spiel.  Programm-Beschreibung: Ein Boot, ein Taucher und die angriffslustige Krake sind auf der Suche und beim Heben der Schatzkiste die Hauptdarsteller. Reicht der Sauerstoff? Und wie kann man dem Kraken entgehen? Vorsicht: Schatzsuche halt Sie in Atem - bis zum letzten Zug.  Und so läuft das Spiel: Über den Auslöseknopf bewegen Sie Ihr Schiff genau über die Schatzkiste, die auf dem Meeresgrund liegt. Der Taucher (Sie bewegen ihn über den Steuerknüppel) muß nun das Seil unter dem Schiff ergreifen, nach unten zur Schatzkiste bringen, dann wieder auftauchen, auf das Schiff klettern und die Kiste heben. Oh - das klingt ganz einfach. Nur da gibt es noch diesen gemeinen Kraken der dem Taucher ganz schön zusetzt und die Schatzkiste dauernd an andere Stellen bringt. Auch der Luftvorrat (Oxygen) reicht nicht unbegrenzt. Drei Versuche gibt es - ob Sie es schaffen, den Schatz zu heben? Viel Spaß und Unterhaltung.  Ein Heimcomputer-Spiel aus dem EUROPA Computer-Club © 1985 MILLER INTERNATIONAL Schallplatten GmbH, 2085 Quickborn bei Hamburg

Name: Fischmarkt
MemoText: Laden des Programmes: Computer einschalten. Programm-Cassette in den Rekorder legen und an den Anfang vorspulen. Dann am Computer die SHIFT- und gleichzeitig die RUN/STOP-Taste drücken. Jetzt die PLAY-Taste am Rekorder betätigen. Der Programm-Name wird angezeigt - jetzt die RETURN-Taste drücken. Erscheint dann nach ca. 5 Minuten das EUROPA-Zeichen, erneut RETURN drücken und man ist im Programm. Sollte der Ladevorgang beim ersten Mal nicht klappen, bitte noch einmal versuchen. Bitte auch immer die Bedienungs-Anleitung des Computer-Herstellers beachten. Beim ATARI-Programm ist der gesamte Ladevorgang auf Spur 2 mit einer Programm-Musik unterlegt.  Programm-Beschreibung (C64) Die wichtigsten Funktionen ergeben sich aus dem Textvorspann zu Beginn des Programmes. Der Spielablauf selbst entspricht dem der ATARI-Version. Programm-Beschreibung (Atari) Im Programm FISCHMARKT wird durch Auslegen von Fanggeräten (grob- und feinmaschige Netze, Reusen) im Meer gefangen und anschließend zu bestmöglichen Preisen auf dem Fischmarkt verkauft. Vor neuer Ausfahrt wird dann jeweils noch Ausrüstung und Zubehör gekauft. Es geht darum, möglichst viel Gewinn zu erzielen. Bis zu 3 Spieler können mitmachen - haben Mitspieler keine Zeit, werden deren Aktivitäten vom Computer übernommen. Kennziffer 'Spieleranzahl 0' bringt eine Spieldemonstration auf den Bildschirm. 1. Vergabe der Fanggebiete Das weiße Fenster wird im Fanggebiet über die Auslösetaste gestoppt (hier wird dann gefischt). Das kostet DM 100,- Gebühr und es beginnt die nächste Phase.  2. Information über Fanggebiete Auslösetaste drücken und über Joystick (links oder rechts) Echolot oder Geräte wählen. Echolot zeigt, was an Fischen vorhanden ist; erneutes Knopfdrücken und Joystick nach rechts läßt die Ausrüstung wählen (grob- und feinmaschige Netze oder Reusen - für Thunfisch, Kabeljau, Hering oder Hummer). Per Knopfdruck Gerät wählen und dann die Anzahl (bis zu 3). Einmal ausgelegte Geräte können über Joystick-Bewegung nach links eingeholt werden. Danach kann mit weißem Fenster eine weitere Echolot-Prüfung vorgenommen und ein Fanggebiet für die nächste Ausfahrt reserviert werden. Auch das kostet eine Gebühr (DM 50,-). Nach den 3 Tätigkeiten AUSLEGEN, EINHOLEN und ECHOLOT ist der nächste Spieler an der Reihe. Übrigens - Joystick nach oben oder unten läßt Tätigkeiten fortsetzen oder abbrechen.  3. Fangtage Es gibt gute und schlechte Tage. Der Fang nimmt mit der Anzahl der ausgelegten Geräte zu.  4. Der Markt Hier wird der Fischfang auf Basis von Tagespreisen verkauft. Die durchschnittlichen Preise sind: Hering 20,- / Thunfisch 40,- / Hummer 100,- und Kabeljau 30,-. In den 4 Markthallen mit Händlern erfährt man die Preise - sagt ein Preis zu, so drückt man die Auslösetaste. Zurück geht es nicht - man kann nur eine Fischart an einen Händler verkaufen. Dann geht es zum Zubehörhändler - die Preise sind immer gleich: feinmaschiges Netz 150,- grobes Netz 200,- Reusen 250,- Je 9 Exemplare können maximal gekauft werden. Joystick nach oben leitet Kauf ein, Menge über links oder rechts und Bestätigung über Auslösetaste. Nicht das Eis vergessen - für 10 Kisten Fisch immer 1 Eisblock einplanen. Je Block 50,- Abgabe nur in 5 Stück-Einheiten.

Name: Denk mit!
MemoText: Laden des Programmes: Computer einschalten. ProgrammCassette in den Rekorder legen und an den Anfang vorspulen. Dann am Computer die SHIFT- und gleichzeitig die RUN/STOP-Taste drücken. Jetzt die PLAY-Taste am Rekorder betätigen. Der Programm-Name wird angezeigt - jetzt die RETURN-Taste drücken. Erscheint dann nach ca. 3 Minuten das EUROPA-Zeichen, erneut RETURN drücken und man ist im Spiel. Sollte der Ladevorgang beim ersten Mal nicht klappen, bitte noch einmal versuchen. Bitte auch immer die Bedienungs-Anleitung des Computer-Herstellers beachten. Beim ATARI-Programm ist der gesamte Ladevorgang auf Spur 2 mit einer Programm-Musik unterlegt.  Programm-Beschreibung Bei diesem Spiel handelt es sich um die Umsetzung des Computer-Klassikers ''Türme von hanoi''. Bis zu fünf unterschiedlich breite Ebenen (im Spiel sind das flinke Männchen) werden über drei Plattformen in möglichst wenig Zügen umsortiert. Es kann niemals eine höhere Anzahl von Männchen über eine geringere Anzahl plaziert werden. Der Computer gibt die geringste Anzahl der Züge vor und registriert die vom Spieler durchgeführten Züge. Gespielt wird über die Tastatur - durch Eingabe der Ausgangsebene (3) und der zwei möglichen Zielebenen (2 oder 1). Viel Spaß und Unterhaltung. Name: Deutschstunde 3, Die
MemoText: BESCHREIBUNG: In diesem Programm werden eingehend die Satzlehre (Syntax) einfacher Sätze behandelt. Sämtliche Satzteile werden mit lateinischen Begriffen (deutsch erklärt!) eingeführt und in Übungssätzen lernen Sie, diese zu bestimmen. Es beginnt mit Subjekt und Prädikat und geht über Objekt und Attribut bis hin zur adverbalen Bestimmung. Zur Erleichterung werden auch die Fragen, die zur eindeutigen Satzteilbestimmung führen jeweils angegeben.  Jedes der drei Programme kann unabhängig von den anderen Teilen genutzt werden, da jeweils ein Teilbereich geschlossen abgehandelt wird.  Jede Programmfolge bietet den Lernstoff von drei vollen Nachhilfestunden!  Ein Heimcomputer-Programm aus dem EUROPA Computer-Club (C) MILLER INTERNATIONAL Schallplatten GmbH, 2085 Quickborn bei Hamburg

Name: Deutschstunde 2, Die
MemoText: BESCHREIBUNG: Ein wichtiges Thema des Deutschunterrichts, das die Schüler bis in die Oberstufe des Gymnasiums beschäftigt, ist die Zeichensetzung. Zunächst wird die Zeichensetzung am Schluß von Sätzen behandelt. Dies ist ohne weitere Grundkenntnisse verständlich. Auch Zeichensetzung bei mehreren Hauptsätzen kann so erlernt werden. Die Zeichensetzung im Satzgefüge aber benötigt Grundkenntnisse in der deutschen Syntax (Satzlehre). Soweit notwendig, werden diese innerhalb eines Exkurses vermittelt. Schließlich werden Satzgefüge in Graphiken deutlich gemacht und erklärt! Name: Shredz64
MemoText: Playing Shredz64 on an emulator ------------------------------- While Shredz64 will certainly run on a C64 emulator, the commands for strumming, lifting the guitar up, and using the whammy bar are sent over the joystick pins normally used for paddles on the C64. Many emulators such as Vice do not support paddles. For the tinkerers out there, if your emulator does support paddles or you're adding support, Shredz64 recognizes the following byte values (in decimal from 0-255):  Pot X: 90 = Strum bar at rest, 21 = strum down, 47 = strum up Pot Y: 44 Whammy Up -> 80 Whammy Down, 19 = Guitar lifted  Additionally, we've noticed timing issues during gameplay, especially if warp mode has previously been used. Name: Bionik Granny Returns
MemoText: Back in 1984, Granny was waiting outside the school gates, waiting to clobber the brats who were responsible for making her life a misery.  Now 26 years later after her hard earned rest, SHE'S BACK. The cantankerous old lady is on a little adventure, which is to go out into town and grab her pension from out of the local post office. Unfortunately for her, the town's full of pushers and shovers. Not only is this bad for her - she's very annoyed. She finds herself in a situation where modern society seems to be too much for her. So she puts on her blue raincoat, picks up her walking cane and gets ready to go out and clobber the poor folk.  Using (or emulating) a joystick in port 2, help Granny clobber passers by with her cane - to retrieve coins. To be able to release a coin, granny must clobber at least five people. If a coin is visible, she can keep clobbering folk and then after the coin has disappeared, she can clobber five people again to release a new coin. Then when a coin has appeared, quickly help Granny grab it. You are not against time in this level. So if you want to do a load of clobbering to boost up your score, then that's what you can do. Out to stop Granny are some people and other beings, throwing or shooting hazards. Avoid those at all costs. After each level has been successfully completed, you will move on to the bonus round. This is where you will have to help the old lady cross the road and enter a building to grab her pension - otherwise something daft will happen. Complete all 8 levels to win the game.
